summary: Intermittent cross-region proxy translation causing SSL handshake retries and inference timeouts for APAC customer
description: Issue summary: BrightLens (dedicated tenant) reports intermittent high tail latency and streaming disconnects during sustained inference traffic. Impact: Customer seeing 5-10% of requests hit 10s+ latencies and some streams terminate with TLS handshake retries, causing client-side reconnects and token duplication. Environment: Production, APAC region behind our edge POPs; Dedicated pool in apac-south-1. Observed start: 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer sends sustained streaming generate requests (chunked SSE) to /v1/streaming with region unset (default routing).
2) Traffic volume ~120 rps from multiple BrightLens app instances over 10–15 minute windows.
3) Observe intermittent failures: client logs show TLS handshake errors and server logs show 499/504 and backend timeouts.
logs: edge-pop logs (apac-south-1) around 2026-03-09T22:04Z: upstream TLS handshake failed: EOF from upstream (envoy ssl) trace_id=trx-8b3f
gateway metrics: 502 spike at 22:04-22:07 UTC; p99 latency jumped from 180ms -> 11.3s
serving-runtime logs: kv-cache miss + extended GC pause observed on worker-17 at 22:05:12 (duration 320ms) but not sufficient to explain 10s tails
timeline: 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC - First customer alert; CS triages and opens ticket
2026-03-09 22:10 UTC - SRE engaged; initial checks of Dedicated pool show normal GPU utilization
2026-03-09 22:20 UTC - Edge team observes transient certificate renegotiations between edge proxy and a west region egress proxy
2026-03-09 22:45 UTC - Temporary mitigation: advised customer to set region_hint=apac-south-1; immediate reduction in TLS retries noted
2026-03-11 09:30 UTC - Deeper traces show requests from APAC routed to us-west-2 via a translation proxy during BGP flap window
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Intermittent BGP path changes caused upstream route to flip to a us-west transit, introducing an additional TLS proxy hop and occasional MTU/mss translation anomalies leading to handshake retransmits.

Hypothesis B: Edge POP affinity snapback (anycast rebalancing) caused some connections to be proxied through a legacy TLS-terminating fleet that lacks the new keepalive tuning, exposing long tail due to TCP/TLS retransmit timeouts.

Trace analysis: Collected 27 traces with trace_id prefix trx-8b3f..trx-8b5a. 7/27 showed an extra hop: edge-pop -> translation-proxy-us-west -> dedicated-gw -> serving-runtime. The extra hop correlates with 9–12s tail latencies.
Packet captures: SYN/SYN-ACK retransmits observed where MSS option dropped after translation-proxy; some clients retried TLS handshake, leading to duplicate streams at application layer.
Config review: The translation-proxy had an older OpenSSL build and a different keepalive/tls-opts profile; also had Nagle enabled and default TCP_USER_TIMEOUT which aggravated the symptom.

Customer impact: Requests that hit the translated path either succeeded after long retry or failed client-side with TLS handshake timeout; roughly 5-10% of active streaming sessions were affected during peak windows.
root_cause_summary: A transient cross-region routing event routed a portion of APAC tenant traffic through a legacy TLS translation proxy in us-west-2. That proxy's TCP/TLS stack and MSS handling caused handshake retransmits and long tail latencies, resulting in streaming disconnects and timeouts for some requests.
resolution: Mitigation: 1) Applied a routing policy change to prefer local apac-south-1 egress for dedicated tenants with region_hint unset; 2) Decommissioned traffic path through legacy translation proxy for affected ASNs; 3) Updated translation-proxy TLS config and enabled keepalives + MSS passthrough. Post-rollback: p99 for BrightLens streams returned to baseline within 45 minutes. Follow-up: full fleet OpenSSL upgrade scheduled, and a permanent route-affinity rule for Dedicated tenants to reduce cross-region translation risk.
postmortem_actions: Schedule OpenSSL rebuild for translation-proxy fleet (ENG-4278)
Add route-affinity test to Chaos/QA that simulates BGP path flips and validates TLS path invariants
Add metric: percent_of_requests_with_extra_proxy_hop (edge->translation->gw) and alert when >0.5%
Update runbook: when customer reports TLS handshake retries, check for translation-proxy hop via traces and advise region_hint as immediate workaround
